cases.question: payment service connection pool exhausted
cases.reference_answer: Kill idle connections holding slots, restart the payment-service pods to reset the pools, and if it recurs increase pool_size or introduce PgBouncer per the connection-pool runbook.

cases.question: The checkout API keeps returning 503s and the payments database seems to be running out of connections. What should I do?
cases.reference_answer: This is connection pool exhaustion: kill idle connections, restart the payment-service pods to reset the pools, and tune pool_size or add PgBouncer if it recurs.

cases.question: How should I choose the connection pool size for a new service?
cases.reference_answer: Size the pool from measured load (peak RPS times average query seconds), set max_overflow to 25-50% of pool_size, and keep pool_size plus max_overflow across all replicas under PostgreSQL max_connections with headroom.

cases.question: customers getting 429 too many requests wrong tier
cases.reference_answer: Check the rate-limit config and per-tier values, correct the tier limits in the configmap, restart the gateway, and clear stale Redis rate-limit counters.

cases.question: Enterprise customers are being throttled even though they are within their plan. How do I fix the gateway config?
cases.reference_answer: Verify the enterprise tier's configured limit, correct the rate-limit config and restart the gateway, then clear the stale Redis counters and confirm the customer's key returns 200s.

cases.question: What are the request-per-minute limits for each API tier?
cases.reference_answer: Free tier is 60 requests/minute (burst 100), standard is 600/minute (burst 1,000), and enterprise is a negotiated floor of 6,000/minute.

cases.question: auth service pods OOMKilled
cases.reference_answer: The service is leaking memory and getting OOMKilled: restart pods to buy time, raise the memory limit short-term, and fix the leak by evicting expired sessions/JWTs or moving the session cache to Redis.

cases.question: Our login service keeps crashing and restarting, and memory climbs until it dies. How do we stop it?
cases.reference_answer: This is a memory leak causing OOMKills: restart pods short-term, raise the memory limit to buy time, and fix the leak by evicting expired sessions/JWTs or moving the session cache to Redis.

cases.question: How do I capture and read a heap dump for a JVM service?
cases.reference_answer: Capture a heap dump with jmap (or -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError), copy it off the pod immediately, and open it in Eclipse MAT or VisualVM, reading the dominator tree for the largest retained objects.

cases.question: disk space critical /var/log full
cases.reference_answer: Identify what is filling the disk, free space by deleting old compressed logs and vacuuming the journal, fix logrotate, and clear old Elasticsearch indices.

cases.question: Our monitoring node is nearly out of disk and Elasticsearch stopped indexing. What do we do?
cases.reference_answer: Free disk immediately (delete old logs, vacuum the journal), fix logrotate, and clear old Elasticsearch indices so it can index again.

cases.question: How do I add log rotation for a new log file?
cases.reference_answer: Drop a logrotate config into /etc/logrotate.d/ via your deploy manifest and test it with logrotate -d (dry run) before shipping.

cases.question: VPN TLS handshake failed certificate expired
cases.reference_answer: The VPN certificate has expired: renew it with certbot --force-renewal, restart the VPN service to load the new cert, verify the new expiry, and enable auto-renewal.

cases.question: All our remote employees suddenly cannot connect to the VPN this morning. Where do I start?
cases.reference_answer: A mass connection failure is typically an expired gateway certificate: renew it with certbot, restart the VPN service, and verify the new certificate.

cases.question: What is the certificate lifetime and renewal policy for VPN gateways?
cases.reference_answer: VPN gateway certificates have a 1-year lifetime and are renewed manually until the appliance supports ACME; an expired production certificate is automatically a SEV-2.

cases.question: Our sign-in system keeps running out of RAM and getting killed. How do we stop it?
cases.reference_answer: The auth service is leaking memory and being OOMKilled: restart pods, raise the limit short-term, and fix the leak by evicting expired sessions/JWTs or moving the cache to Redis.
